---
title: "Read the record of a Kapso build with kapso trace"
sidebarTitle: "Read the record"
description: "kapso trace lays a finished campaign out section by section: every attempt with its sessions and runs, the lessons served and used, what was voided or rejected and on what evidence, the sessions that failed, and the delivered candidate. Text for a person, --json for a script."
keywords: ["kapso trace", "campaign record", "session record", "run entries", "hooks", "delegates", "voided attempt", "safe to merge", "trace --json"]
---

A build writes everything it does under `campaign/.kapso/`. `kapso trace`
reads it back after the fact, without the agent that ran it, and lays the
evidence out so a reader can answer six questions from the record alone:
what won, why, what was voided and on what evidence, what was rejected
and why, what it cost, and whether it is safe to merge.

```bash
kapso trace campaign                          # every section, the attempts compact
kapso trace campaign --branch generic_exp_1   # one attempt with its evidence in full
kapso trace campaign --json                   # the same as data
```

```python
view = Kapso.trace("campaign")
print(view.explain())        # the text
view.data                    # the JSON
view.attempts                # one entry per node
view.delivered               # the delivered candidate, None when none succeeded
```

A campaign still running renders too, marked `partial` with the reason
(the phase it is in, the error it failed with, no status yet, or waiting
on you with the count of requests); follow a live one with
[`kapso watch`](/docs/build/run-and-watch#watch). A directory with no
`.kapso/` inside is not a campaign and is refused by name.

The trace above is a real one, from the trading example's recorded build
of 2026-10-25, abridged: a trading build whose first
attempt scored a Sharpe of 2.16 and was voided because a development
script had read the hold-out window, and whose second was cut by the time
budget. Where each answer sits:

| Question | Where |
|---|---|
| What won | The header's `delivered` line and the `DELIVERED` section: the branch, the commit, the files its branch changed against the seed, the judge's verdict in a line (`--branch` for the words in full) |
| Why | The attempt's `evaluation`, `verification` and `judge` lines; `--branch` prints the judge's feedback and the verifier's summary whole |
| What was voided, on what evidence | `VOIDED OR REJECTED`: the verifier's verdict with each finding, the rule and the evidence as the verifier wrote them |
| What was rejected and why | The same section: an integrity rejection with the evaluator's output, or the judge's invalidation |
| What it cost | The header's `cost`, each attempt's figure, each run's; `cost` says when the figure covers the Claude Code sessions only (Codex reports none) and how many runs ended with no cost figure |
| Safe to merge | `DELIVERED`: the verification, the integrity line, the hooks that fired in its sessions and which were denied (or that none was staged, or that a host reports no hook events), the failures in its sessions. The trace prints the evidence and no verdict; the conclusion is the reader's |

Each attempt lists its sessions in the order they ran: the ideation of
its iteration, the implementation on its branch, the verification and the
judge. A session has one line per run the host made for it, a resumed or
retried session two or more; the line carries how the run ended
(`success`, `error`, `timeout`, `paused` for a session the inbox stopped,
`refused` for an answer the model's safeguards refused), its duration,
its cost, its turns, the tools it used, the gates it called, the hooks
that fired and how many denied, the delegates it asked; a run that
resumed the session says why (`retry: tags missing` on a judge's second
run). An attempt the budget left unjudged says so on its `judge` line.
`OTHER SESSIONS` holds the sessions that belong to no attempt: the
harness setup, the engine's own inference sessions, and a node still in
flight. `LESSONS` is one entry per source served, with who
read which cards and which the judge found load-bearing per node;
`SESSIONS FAILED` lists every run that ended `error`, `timeout` or
`refused`, and names the kinds of which every run failed.

## One attempt in full

```bash
kapso trace campaign --branch generic_exp_0
```

The same sections, with the one attempt's evidence whole: the idea, each
run's model and host session, its error, each hook's decision and reason,
each delegate's report, the files it changed and its closing message; the
evaluator's output; the verifier's summary and findings; the judge's
feedback. The data behind `--json` always carries all of it; `--branch`
is how the text shows it.

## The data

`--json` prints what `Kapso.trace(path).data` holds, and
`TraceView(data)` renders the same text again from it. A script or a
skill reads the keys as pinned:

```text
schema_version   2
campaign         the directory
state            complete | partial
branch           the branch the view is narrowed to, or null
header           objective, harness, experience (one label per source), evaluator,
                 budget {elapsed_min, total_min, reserve_min},
                 budget_source (which budget won when the brief and the launch both named minutes),
                 cost {usd, coverage (the hosts the figure covers: all, or claude_code when a Codex
                       session ran), unpriced_runs (Claude Code runs whose spend no figure covers:
                       killed before their result, and not resumed in a run that reported one)},
                 stopped_reason, stop_detail, stop_note (the sentence a budget stop ended on: the
                 admission refusal or the finishing cut), experiments, rejected,
                 delivered {branch, commit}, status {state, phase, error},
                 requests (what the person must answer when the campaign paused)
attempts[]       node, parent, branch, commit (the branch head when the attempt was evaluated;
                 null when it never was), unjudged ("" when judged, else the reason),
                 idea, sessions[] {label, module, host, hooks_staged, runs[]},
                 evaluation {score, valid, provenance, integrity_error, output},
                 verification {verdict, summary, findings} | null,
                 judge {stop, valid, feedback}, cards {read, listed, load_bearing},
                 cost_usd, duration_seconds
sessions[]       the sessions that belong to no attempt, the same shape
lessons[]        reference, kind, provenance, head, served, read_by {session: [cards]},
                 load_bearing_by {node: [cards]}
voided[]         node, branch, reason, evidence[]
failures[]       label, module, host, exit, error, every_run
delivered        branch, commit, base_commit, files_changed, verification, feedback | null
```

A run entry, as the session record holds it: `started`, `ended`,
`duration_seconds`, `deadline_seconds` (the deadline the run was
launched with: its room under the budget or its configured timeout;
`null` without one), `model`, `cli_session_id`, `exit`, `error`,
`retry_reason` (set on a run that resumed the session: `tags missing`
for the judge's retry),
`cost_usd` (this run's share of the host's cumulative figure),
`cost_cumulative`, `turns`, `usage` (the host's token counts), `tools`
(by name), `gates` (by server, by tool), `hooks` (each with its event,
name, decision and reason, a hook that blocked a tool call included;
`null` where the host reports none),
`delegates` (each with its name, status, usage and report; on Codex the
collaboration calls, by verb), `host_errors`, `files_changed` (the files
the session wrote through its editing tools, relative to its directory;
a file written by a shell command shows in the branch's diff instead),
`last_message`. The delivered candidate's `files_changed` are the files
its branch changed against the seed, from the diff.

## Where each file lives

```text
campaign/.kapso/
├── solution.json                    the record Solution.open reads
├── status.json                      what kapso watch reads
├── run_state.json                   the checkpoint: every node with its evaluation, verification and feedback
├── launch.json                      every flag of the launch
├── sessions/<session>/session.json  the session's record: what it was staged with, and its runs
├── sessions/<session>/stream.jsonl  the host's own event stream, where a delegate's report is in full
├── serving/serving-record.yaml      what the campaign was served, each source at its pinned head
├── serving/serving-pull.jsonl       the pull log: every bank read, by session
└── verification/<branch>/           diff.patch, evaluation_output.txt, verdict.json per verified attempt
```

The session labels are the branch for an implementation session,
`verification/<branch>` and `feedback/<branch>` for its verifier and its
judge, `ideation/iter<n>/<member>` for the ideation of iteration `n`,
`difficulties/<branch>` for the reconstruction of what an attempt lost,
`harness_setup` for the setup session, and `engine/<role>/<n>` for the
engine's own inference sessions (the repo-memory bootstrap, the commit
messages), which belong to no attempt. The trace joins the sessions to
their attempts by these labels (a node records the iteration that made
it, and every node of an iteration shares its ideation session) and the
pull log's events by the session the gate served.
